propositions: Escaped-defect measurement is incomplete: only 1.1% of 648 bugs have detected_by metadata, preventing calculation of true bug-escape rate or detection-stage efficiency.

Plan-review adoption and governance artifact compliance (ticket trailers, DCO, Change-Id) rose from near-zero in Q2 to ~100% by late August, but first-pass review rate remains 49.0% with median p90 attempts of 8, consuming 114.72 LLM calls per completion-PASS.

Completion verdicts show 72.3% first-pass across 998 tickets; tickets with Testing-section headings and explicit file-impact declarations correlate with higher first-pass rates (79.7% and 74.2% respectively), suggesting process signaling value.

Caused_by attribution links are advisory and demonstrably noisy: larger diffs are more likely to receive blame attribution, and the top 8-bug fan-in source is semantically mixed, creating false-positive risk that confounds source-ticket risk assessment.

Code health risks persist: 35 modules at or above 720 LOC (15 at 780+), 4.09% duplication, and 47.7% same-file retouch within 24h indicate debt pressure and coordination hotspots; source diffs became smaller and test co-change increased from Q2 to Q3, supporting process maturation.
